title: Enroll in E-Verify and verify new hires (South Carolina)
authority: South Carolina employment eligibility law / U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
description: South Carolina requires all private employers to use E-Verify for new hires.

feeDetail.note: There is no fee to file or register.

penalty.note: Older sources list a civil penalty of $100 to $1,000 per employee not verified, plus license suspension for knowing violations.
